name: Nebo-M
note: 55Zh6M Nebo-M mobile multiband counter-stealth radar complex: a VHF-band RLM-M, L-band RLM-D and S-band RLM-S AESA, networked through the RLM-KU command post on BAZ-6909 8x8 chassis. Designed to detect low-observable, hypersonic and ballistic targets and cue SAM batteries (S-400 etc.).

source.title: 55Zh6M Nebo-M TALL RACK mobile multi-band radar complex | GlobalSecurity.org
source.note: Complex 'scans airspace at a range of 1,800 km and an altitude of 1,200 km'. That is the instrumented ceiling against large/high targets; export figures are quoted 600-1,800 km. Against a stealth fighter the VHF RLM-M module is claimed by Almaz-Antey to detect 5th-gen aircraft at only ~100-200 km (unverified).

name: AN/TPY-2
note: Army-Navy Transportable Radar Surveillance, an X-band missile-defence radar developed with THAAD. Runs in Forward-Based Mode (early ascent-phase cueing) or Terminal Mode (co-located with a THAAD battery). Aperture 9.2 m2 with 25,344 T/R modules. A ballistic-missile sensor, not an aircraft surveillance radar.

source.title: AN/TPY-2 Radar | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 'Reportedly capable of tracking objects at ranges 870 to 3,000 km depending on target and mode.' 3,000 km applies to forward-based cueing of large ballistic objects; ~870 km-class in terminal mode. Surface-based but points high, so the horizon limit does not bite for exo-atmospheric targets.

source.title: AN/TPY-2 Radar | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: In a 1998 test the radar accurately tracked 'over 180 separate objects and debris'. Used here as an indicative simultaneous-track figure; the true capacity is classified.

name: JY-27A
note: CETC JY-27A, a mobile VHF-band 3D long-range air-surveillance and guidance radar using an active phased array, marketed as a counter-stealth / early-warning sensor.

source.title: JY-27A | Radartutorial
source.note: Instrumented range 310 NM (500 km); 'able to detect stealth aircraft like the F-22 at a distance of up to 500 km'. Against a conventional target this is the instrumented limit; against genuine low-observables the effective range is lower (~350 km per vendor material).

name: Air surveillance radar (generic)
note: Generic placeholder representing a modern medium/high-altitude 3D air-surveillance radar (in the class of Ground Master 400, 36D6, TRML-3D). Not a specific fielded system; figures are representative estimates for map-modelling only.

source.title: Generic / representative figure
source.note: Typical instrumented range of a modern 3D air-surveillance radar against a fighter-sized (~1-5 m2) target at altitude. Not a specific system; substitute a real radar's figure where one is known.

source.title: Generic / representative figure
source.note: Representative simultaneous-track capacity for a modern surveillance radar; not a measured value.

source.title: Generic / representative figure
source.note: Assumed antenna height ~10 m (typical mast/vehicle mount) for the radar-horizon calculation; adjust to the real emplacement.

name: Over-the-horizon radar
note: Generic placeholder for a skywave over-the-horizon (OTH) radar (in the class of Australia's JORN, Russia's Container/29B6, or the US ROTHR). Uses ionospheric refraction to see far beyond the geometric horizon, so it is NOT horizon-limited, but resolution is coarse (tens of km) and it has a large skip-zone dead area near the site. Figures are representative estimates only.

source.title: Generic / representative figure
source.note: Skywave OTH radars typically cover ~1,000-3,000 km (beyond a near-site skip zone of several hundred km); 2,500 km taken as a mid figure. Not a specific system, and coverage varies strongly with ionospheric conditions and time of day.
